title: Every Spark Liquidity Layer deployment is registered as a uniform Instance Configuration Document rather than bespoke prose
content:
Across A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.4 through A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.4.3, every single deployment of the Spark Liquidity Layer — Aave on Avalanche, Spark Savings v2 on Robinhood Chain and X Layer, Blackrock, Centrifuge, Morpho — is expressed as an "Instance Configuration Document" with the *same* fixed subdocument slots:

1. `RRC Framework Full Implementation` (a status flag)
2. `Parameters` → `Instance Identifiers` (network, target protocol, asset supplied, token) and `Contract Addresses`
3. `Rate Limit IDs` and `Rate Limits`
4. `Off-chain Operational Parameters`
5. `Instance-specific Operational Processes` / `Instance-specific Operational Parameters`

The slots are present even when empty or unresolved. The Avalanche Spark Savings v2 USDC instance still carries a `Rate Limits` section whose entire content is "The specific `maxAmount` and `slope` for this conduit's inflow/outflow are not defined for this Instance" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.4.2.1.2.4).

This is the load-bearing design choice: by forcing every venue into an identical schema, the Artifact converts a portfolio of structurally dissimilar integrations (a lending market, a tokenized treasury fund, a savings vault) into rows of one table. Coverage gaps become *visible absences* in a known slot rather than silent omissions, and a reviewer can diff two instances without understanding either protocol. The cost is verbosity — the majority of the Artifact's text is empty or placeholder scaffolding.
description: A fixed slot template — RRC status, identifiers, contract addresses, rate limit IDs, rate limits, off-chain params, instance-specific processes — makes heterogeneous venues diffable and auditable.
